summary: Francis Louis Noël Goré specialized in Tibetology and religious studies, studying at the Séminaire des Missions Étrangères de Paris (~1904–1907) and College General (~1907). He served with the Tibet Mission as vicaire apostolique and procureur at Tsechung (1931–1952).

Francis N. J. is a scholar of Indology and history and archaeology. He earned a Master's in Ancient History at the University of Calicut and completed doctoral studies under M. R. Raghava Varier (attested 2002).

Working in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies, Francis Vincent Tiso earned degrees from Cornell, Harvard Divinity School, Columbia, and Union Theological Seminary. He held teaching posts at Columbia, the Archdiocese of San Francisco, Sapienza University of Rome, and Pontifical Gregorian University.

Francis Whyte Ellis worked in Indology and linguistics. He served in the East India Company (~1796–1819), the Madras Civil Service (1796), and the Board of Revenue (1802), held a Collector post at the University of Madras (1810), and founded College of Fort St. George Press (1812).

Francis Wilford worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He served in the military for the East India Company (1781–1794), was a fellow member of The Asiatic Society (~1790–1822), and served as Secretary to the committee at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

Francis William Bain was a scholar in Indology and history and archaeology who studied at Westminster School and Christ Church, Oxford (~1882–1889). He served in the Indian Civil Service and was Professor of History and Political Economy at Deccan College (~1892–1919).

Francis Woodman Cleaves worked in Sinology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Dartmouth and Harvard, as well as under Paul Pelliot, before serving as a professor at Harvard University from 1941 to 1980.

Francis X. Clooney works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. Educated at Fordham and the University of Chicago, he held posts at Boston College (1984–2005), the Oxford Centre for Hindu Studies (~2005–2007), and Harvard University, including Parkman Professor of Divinity (2005) and Director (2010).

Francis Younghusband was a specialist in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied at Clifton College and the Royal Military College, Sandhurst, and held an appointment in the Foreign and Political Department in 1889.

Francisco García Ayuso was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied under Martin Haug at the University of Munich. His career included posts at the Conciliar Seminary of Ávila, Complutense University of Madrid, and Escuela Superior de Comercio.

Francisco María Rivero y Godoy was an Indologist who earned his doctorate at the Complutense University of Madrid by 1866. He subsequently served there from 1877 to 1881 as its first Professor of Sanskrit.

Francisco Varela worked in philosophy and Buddhist studies, earning degrees at the University of Chile and Harvard. He held appointments at the University of Chile, University of Colorado Denver, École Polytechnique, CNRS, Pitié-Salpêtrière Hospital, and the University of Paris.

Francisco Xavier de Santa Anna was an Indologist and linguist. He became a Father in the Order of Discalced Carmelites in 1790 and served as Apostolic Vicar of the Archdiocese of Verapoly from 1831 to 1844.
Francisco de Montoliú y Togores worked in Indology and religious studies. He served as a Professor at the Technical University of Madrid and founded the Theosophical Society in Spain in 1889.

id: P:Francisco de Paula Canalejas y Casas
summary: Francisco de Paula Canalejas y Casas was a scholar in linguistics and Indology who completed his doctorate at Complutense University of Madrid in 1858. He served as Professor of Literature at the University of Valladolid (1860–1862) and as extraordinary professor at Complutense University.

Franciscus Verellen is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who earned doctorates at Oxford and the EPHE under Kristofer Schipper. He taught at EPHE and Columbia before serving as Director of the École française d'Extrême-Orient (1991–2021).

Franciszek Krček was a linguist who earned his doctorate from the University of Lviv (~1888–1893) and studied under Josef Zubatý at Charles University, Leipzig, and Berlin. In 1909, he became a Docent at the University of Lviv.

Franciszek Ksawery Malinowski was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Warsaw (~1827–1830) and the Major Seminary of Pelplin (1829). In 1873, he became a member of the Polish Academy of Arts and Sciences.

Franciszek Machalski specialized in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies, earning a Ph.D. at the University of Lviv under Stefan Bołeslaw Stasiak. He served as an assistant at Lviv (~1930–1934) and extraordinary professor at Jagiellonian University (1951–1974).

Franciszek Tokarz was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Lviv and Jagiellonian University under Jan Szczepan Otrębski, Stefan Bołeslaw Stasiak, and Helena Willman-Grabowska. He taught Sanskrit at the John Paul II Catholic University of Lublin from 1954 to 1970.
